## Argentina from Buenos Aires to Patagonia, Iguazú and the northwest

After Mendoza, you head into Patagonia. In El Calafate, the Perito Moreno Glacier is the main attraction. Its wall of ice rises above the water, and from the viewpoints you can watch blocks of ice break away. The scenery then changes completely as you visit the subtropical forest and Iguazú Falls from the Argentine and Brazilian sides. Here, you’ll find heat, humid air, dense greenery and dozens of cascades around the main drop, the Devil’s Throat.

The last leg takes you through northwestern Argentina. Vineyards reappear in Cafayate, this time amid dry mountain landscapes. The road then leads through high-altitude Los Cardones National Park and the Quebrada de Humahuaca, past the Hill of Seven Colours at Purmamarca and on to the white expanse of the Salinas Grandes salt flats. Over 15 days, the itinerary takes in the capital, the wine regions, Patagonia, Iguazú and the northwestern Andes.
